plain.text: Jacob called his sons together to tell them what would happen to them in days to come. Reuben, the firstborn, was unstable as water and would not excel, because he had defiled his father's bed. Simeon and Levi's anger and violence were cursed; they would be scattered in Israel. Judah would be praised by his brothers; "the sceptre will not depart from Judah" until the one comes to whom it belongs, and the nations will obey him. Jacob gave short sayings about Zebulun, Issachar, Dan, Gad, Asher and Naphtali. Joseph was a fruitful vine; though archers attacked him, his bow stayed steady because of the Mighty One of Jacob, the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel, who would bless him richly. Benjamin was like a ravenous wolf. These are the twelve tribes of Israel, each given an appropriate blessing.

Jacob instructed them to bury him with his fathers in the cave of Machpelah, where Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, and Leah were buried. When Jacob finished, he drew his feet up into the bed, breathed his last, and was gathered to his people.

summary.bigIdea: Before he dies, Jacob speaks over each of his twelve sons, who become the twelve tribes of Israel.
points: Jacob speaks honestly about each son's character and future.
Judah is promised a royal sceptre; many Christians read this as pointing to the Messiah.
Jacob asks to be buried with his family in Canaan, and dies.
summary.reflection: Jacob's words reflected each son's choices. What would you like your character to be known for?
